The planet with the highest density is the one with the same composition as Earth but 5 times more massive. For planets of similar composition, greater mass leads to stronger gravitational compression, increasing bulk density above Earth's value (~5.5 g/cm³). The Earth-like planet in (a) and the explicitly stated density in (b) are both ~5.5 g/cm³, while the half-mass planet in (d) would be less compressed and thus less dense.

Answer: A
